note: Independent oracle for the N-AALP C4 identity RECORD + THREAD surfaces (design.md §5.2/§5.3/§5.4/§5.5, R-1.4/R-5.2/R-5.3/R-5.4, spec/naalp-draft-01.cddl naalp-revocation/naalp-foreign-link/naalp-rotation): RevocationRecord, RevokedAt, VerifyRevocation, ForeignLinkRecord, VerifyForeignLink, RotationEvidence, Thread, Thread.Attributable, ResolveThread. Go (impl/go/identity) and Rust (impl/rust/src/identity.rs) MUST reproduce every *_hex byte and every expect_valid/expect_linked/expect_error/expect_revoked/expect_thread/expect verdict. Real §5.1 self-certifying signer ids (via signerid_oracle's independent multicodec/multihash/multibase construction) are used for RevocationRecord.key and RotationRecord.old/new, the fields later CheckSigner'd against a pubkey; opaque worked labels are used for ForeignLinkRecord.controls/foreign_id, which are not. VerifyRevocation grades a deployer-configured recovery-key authorization set (§5.3), fail-closed; impl/go and impl/rust implement it (see the file docstring). Generated by tools/identity_records_oracle.py; do not hand-edit.

record_bytes.name: real_id_small_notafter
record_bytes.note: key is the REAL §5.1 self-certifying id of SEED_E; small not_after (1-byte uint)

record_bytes.name: real_id_epoch_notafter
record_bytes.note: same key, epoch-ms-scale not_after (8-byte uint head) — width sensitivity

record_bytes.name: opaque_label_notafter_zero
record_bytes.note: Bytes() is a pure CBOR encoder — agnostic to whether `key` is a real derived id; not_after=0 edge case

verify.name: valid_self_revoked
verify.note: §5.3: signed by the key it revokes, no recovery key configured -> valid

verify.name: valid_self_with_recovery_configured
verify.note: §5.3: the revoked key signs while a recovery key is ALSO configured -> still valid; the recovery set does not perturb the self-signature path

verify.name: recovery_key_valid_per_design
verify.note: §5.3: 'signed by the key (or a deployer-configured recovery key)'. K_R's id is in authorized_recovery_ids, so a revocation of K_E signed by K_R is VALID. impl/go and impl/rust implement this (Shawn approved option (a), 2026-08-21).

verify.name: recovery_key_not_configured_reject
verify.note: FAIL-CLOSED anchor: the SAME K_R signature, but no recovery key is configured (authorized_recovery_ids empty) -> SignerMismatch. Proves the recovery path is authorization-gated, not accept-any-valid-signature.

verify.name: wrong_key_reject
verify.note: even with K_R configured as a recovery key, a revocation signed by an UNRELATED third key K_G (neither the revoked key nor a configured recovery id) -> SignerMismatch (§5.5). Proves 'recovery configured' != 'accept any signer'.

verify.name: tampered_signature_reject
verify.note: correct key/id, corrupted signature bytes -> reject (authorized signer, bad signature; no design-named kind beyond 'reject')

verify.name: recovery_signer_tampered_sig_reject
verify.note: CHECK-ORDER anchor: K_R is a configured recovery id (authorization passes) but its signature is corrupted -> reject. Proves the signature is still verified after the membership check on the recovery path too.

record_bytes.name: nfc_form
record_bytes.note: foreign_id in NFC form (the CDDL-required form)

record_bytes.name: nfd_form_different_bytes
record_bytes.note: SAME logical identity string in NFD form -> DIFFERENT bytes (Bytes() is a pure encoder; the NFC requirement is enforced by VerifyForeignLink, not by Bytes())

verify.name: valid_unexpired
verify.note: valid cross-signature under the FOREIGN key, before not_after -> linked

verify.name: at_boundary_still_linked
verify.note: now == not_after -> not yet expired (uniform not_after boundary convention)

verify.name: expired_ignored
verify.note: §5.5: expired -> link ignored, no error, object stays valid on its own signature

verify.name: wrong_key_ignored
verify.note: §5.5: cross-signature does not verify under the candidate key -> link ignored

verify.name: non_nfc_foreign_id_rejected
verify.note: CDDL: foreign_id MUST be NFC (else NonNFC) — checked before expiry/signature

resolve.name: single_link
resolve.note: one rotation A->B -> Root=A, Current=B, Chain=[A,B]

resolve.name: contiguous_chain_3
resolve.note: A->B->C->D, three rotations -> Root=A, Current=D, Chain=[A,B,C,D]

resolve.name: broken_link_old_mismatch
resolve.note: second link's old != first link's new (id_broken != id_b) — each link is individually validly self-signed, but the chain does not connect -> RotationUnauthorized from the CONTIGUITY guard, before any co-signature check on the second link

resolve.name: broken_link_forged_old_signature
resolve.note: second link's old DOES equal the first link's new (contiguous), but the old leg is signed by the WRONG key (SEED_X, not SEED_B) -> RotationUnauthorized from the CO-SIGNATURE guard, isolating it from the contiguity guard
